pairs.difference: A: the backboard is turned so its right edge is nearer, and top and bottom edges converge gently to the left. Rim, net and pole all share that view, and the pole is cropped by the card edge. The 0.699 planar share comes from the big flat board and sits just above the real range. B: the atom floats dead centre, seen almost head-on, with no ground. Its sphere is a smooth rainbow. The orbit tubes keep the same thickness all the way round, so they barely foreshorten as they go behind it.
pairs.fix: Turn the atom about 20 degrees and look slightly down on it. Make each orbit ring thinner and smaller where it passes behind the sphere and thicker where it passes in front. Crop nothing, but add a soft contact shadow so it sits in space.

pairs.difference: A: the ring box has a clear, mild three-quarter high view. Top faces, lid interior and base all read as flat patches at one angle. B: the jetpack is nearly frontal with a slight roll. The red bottom caps show from below while the shoulder cones and straps read as straight-on, so the tanks do not settle on one camera height. They swell into smooth rainbow cylinders with few flat faces (0.043).
pairs.fix: Show the jetpack in a three-quarter view from slightly above. Show the top of the tank shoulders and hide the undersides of the bottom caps. Turn both tanks, straps and buckles the same way.

pairs.difference: A: the whole dome sits centred at a low, level eye height, with a thin strip of grass, flat distant hills and clouds, and a simple front-on view. Like the generated lighthouses, it fits the whole object in the frame instead of cropping it. B: the motel sign has a low camera, and the posts and porch uprights lean together. Building, fence, tree and sky give several depth layers with the sign out in front, matching the deep real scenes such as the bike and taxi. Planar share is slightly above the real range but is explained by flat signs and walls.
pairs.fix: Turn the dome building about 20 degrees and move in so its base is cropped by the bottom edge. Add a near foreground object overlapping it, and keep the hills soft and far behind.

pairs.difference: A: the bottle floats tilted with a mild view, showing a little of the cap top, and the sunburst gives no ground. B: the water polo goal has a high camera. The pool plane reads as one even colour in the lens, and posts, net and ball all stand on it with reflections. Perspective is moderate and the sides recede consistently. Neither card breaks its view.

A: the flower bed has a high camera, a straight horizon line, and a stone ring that opens as one even ellipse on the flat floor. B: the stacked books have a three-quarter view with top faces and page ends as flat patches, and a sill, drawer and window as simpler background layers behind. Both hold one camera, and neither shows forced perspective.

A: the tape cabinet is a tall box seen from above in a wide-angle view. Its side face tapers hard toward the feet, and the tile floor lines fan out. It stands free and whole on a floor with a flat icon wall behind. B: the computer has the same placement as the real computer in the lessons, with mild perspective, a straight desk edge cut by the card, and flat, even face patches. The view is shared by monitor, keyboard and mouse.
pairs.fix: Draw the cabinet from near its front-panel height with its vertical edges almost parallel, and show less of the top. Stand it on a straight table edge running across the card, with a simple background.

pairs.difference: A: the binoculars lie on planks seen from high up, with no horizon and a tilted floor filling the card. The perspective is strong, as the near lenses are much larger than the eyepieces, but barrels, bridge and planks agree. B: the robot arm stands on tiles with a straight horizon splitting the card, like the lessons' generated flat ground band. The joint discs face the viewer almost flat while the base is seen from above, so the arm looks like a side view on a top-viewed base.
pairs.fix: Turn the arm and its base together in a three-quarter view, so the joint discs become ellipses that match the base's angle. Lower the camera so less of the tile floor shows.

pairs.difference: A: the car mixes views. The hover discs show their glowing undersides from below, while the cabin, seats and steering wheel read from above and the hood reads from the front. In the lens the discs turn magenta (facing down) under a green top. B: the scarf is seen front-on with its collar loop and tails in one consistent frontal view, and needs no ground.
pairs.fix: Pick one camera slightly above the car in a three-quarter front view. Show only thin edges of the hover discs under the body, not their full undersides, with the seats and hood seen from that same height.

pairs.difference: A: the ice tray has a high three-quarter view, with a fairly strong near corner and even top faces, and sits on a wood plane tilted slightly off level. B: the phone has a high three-quarter view on tiles, and the lens shows the floor edge bending a little, as on the lessons' generated round tables, but the phone itself keeps one view. Neither gives a firm reason.

A: the plane has a banking three-quarter view with the nose near and the tail far. Wings and engines agree, and clouds stand in soft layers in front of and behind it, so depth is real. B: the satellite floats with its underside showing and the box seen from below, while the dish is tipped to show its inner bowl from above. The two panels sit at different turns, and the only depth is a flat patterned background.
pairs.fix: Keep one camera slightly above the satellite: hide the bottom face and show the top of the box. Turn both solar panels to the same angle and put soft clouds or a planet edge behind it for depth.

pairs.difference: A: the shoes have a three-quarter view from above, a straight floor line, and both shoes turned the same way, standing firmly on the floor. B: the flask is almost front-on on a shelf with its top strip and front face as flat bands. Its liquid ellipse agrees with a slightly raised eye. Each is consistent, and the shelf's simple layers match real cards.

A: the tube is whole and centred. The cap rim is nearly flat while the base rings open wide, which implies a strong perspective change over a small object. It stands on a tile floor with a flat wall behind, and the floor and wall seam sits at a slight angle in the lens. B: the dock has a high camera with the deck receding through water to the beach. Posts, ring and rope sit on one consistent water plane, with several depth layers and overlap.
pairs.fix: Draw the tube with a gentler view, with base and cap rings opening by a similar small amount. Cut it off at the card edge or overlap it with a near foreground console, and make the wall simpler and softer behind it.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away by showing the whole object centred and free-standing, rather than cropped or overlapped in a scene. They look down too much, with forced near corners and keystoned boxes. Their ground is a simple flat band with a straight or slightly curved horizon, and the background is a flat pattern rather than real depth layers. Parts also slip between views, such as undersides seen from below under tops seen from above, or panels turned differently. Caveat: most test calls are low confidence on view alone. For those, the sci-fi subject (the run is the sci-fi set) nudged my choice, so subject matter is a prior here, not a viewpoint finding. p06 is the firmest, because card B matches the real lesson computer.
